paragraphs: StepFun Step is a family of models from the developer StepFun, offered through the StepFun API Platform. StepFun says step-5-preview is the flagship model for agentic work, step-3.7-flash is a high-speed multimodal reasoning model, step-3.5-flash is a high-speed model for agent and coding tasks, and step-3.5-flash-2603 is a version optimized for high-frequency agent scenarios. The family also includes speech models such as stepaudio-2.5-tts, a next-generation contextual TTS model, and stepaudio-2.5-asr, a next-generation automatic speech recognition model, plus step-router-v1, a smart routing model that dispatches requests by task complexity. StepFun says more StepFun flagship models will be added over time.

StepFun offers these models in two ways. The standard API channel has its own quota and pay-as-you-go pricing. Step Plan is a subscription service from the StepFun API Platform that lets you use StepFun models at a subscription price in coding tools and agent platforms such as OpenClaw, Claude Code, Trae, and Cursor. Step Plan uses Credits as its unified billing unit, with four tiers named Flash Mini, Flash Plus, Flash Pro, and Flash Max, and booster packs available when the monthly allowance runs out. StepFun says every tier provides the same high-speed model performance.

price_limits.summary: Across the 3 versions, input prices run from $0.1 to $1 per million tokens and output prices from $0.3 to $2.7. Step 3.5 Flash is the cheapest, at $0.1 per million input tokens and $0.3 per million output tokens. Step 5 Preview has the largest context window, 1,000,000 tokens.

family_reading.text: StepFun Step is a small family, with 2 versions in the OpenRouter catalog, and both publish open weights and support reasoning. Both offer a 262144 token context window, and both accept image, text and video input while returning text. The newest version, Step 3.7 Flash, allows up to 230400 output tokens at $0.2 per million input and $1.15 per million output. The earlier Step 3.5 Flash caps output at 65536 tokens but costs less, $0.1 input and $0.3 output. The facts suggest the family suits long-context work over mixed media, especially tasks needing reasoning and very long answers, and open weights help those who self-host. The limits are the narrow version spread and the higher output price of the newer tier.
